subject: Exhibit H — SKU attribute reconciliation & pro-rata floor/cap mechanics (redlines)
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@brightpath.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.z@brightpath.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Reconcile Exhibit H SKU attributes + pro-rata treatment?

Mina — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The BrightPath procurement team has two open questions we need clarified before legal can sign the order form: 

1) SKU attribute mapping: Exhibit H currently maps "packaging" at the SKU level, but our internal billing SKU is an attribute combination (model_size + priority_tier). When we migrate some workloads mid-quarter we need a clear rule for converting between attributes so our invoice matches usage. Can Redwood provide a deterministic conversion formula (example row from sku-mapping-comparison.csv attached)?

2) Pro-rata floor/cap during SKU migrations: the redline attached to Exhibit H adds a floor/cap corridor that seems absolute (fixed min/max per SKU). That would penalize us when we migrate customers from a legacy SKU to a new, more efficient SKU mid-billing-period. Can we agree to a pro-rata true-up rule which: 
  - prorates by hours in period, and
  - for migrations that change the billing metric (e.g., tokens -> request-units) applies a 30-day rolling conversion window rather than a hard floor?

We'd like to avoid asking legal for multiple passes — Emily is on copy and can share their in-house redline. If you can reply with the simplest editable wording, we can loop legal.

Thanks,
Jordan Park
Procurement Manager, BrightPath Analytics
[Attachment: sku-mapping-comparison.csv]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.z@brightpath.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reconcile Exhibit H SKU attributes + pro-rata treatment?

Jordan — appreciate the clear note and example CSV. I reviewed with Karthik (legal) and the product team. Quick answers up front, followed by a proposed clean redline attached: 

Short answers:
- SKU mapping: we can include a deterministic conversion table in Exhibit H that ties Redwood SKU_id -> (model_size, priority_tier) and a documented conversion algorithm. That will be part of the attachment called "sku-mapping-comparison.csv" in the draft.
- Pro-rata during migrations: Redwood is fine with a prorated hours-in-period approach for migrations that leave the billing metric unchanged. For metric conversions (e.g., tokens -> request-units) we propose a "conversion smoothing" window: use a 30-day rolling average to align usage between old and new metrics, with final reconciliation at the next monthly invoice.

Proposed changes in the attached Exhibit-H_REDLINE_v3.docx (high level):
- Replace the absolute "Cap" language with an "Adaptive Corridor" definition that references a rolling 30-day baseline when SKU attribute conversion occurs.
- Add a short algorithmic example demonstrating prorate_by_hours(t_1,t_2) + conversion_factor derivation.
- Add an operational note that invoicing will include a line-item: "SKU_migration_trueup" and that dispute windows are 60 days post-invoice.

I've attached our suggested redline (v3) for legal to review. If BrightPath prefers quarterly reconciliation instead of monthly finalization we can accommodate that, but monthly is our default to keep billing aligned.

Next steps:
- If the redline looks good to you, we can have Karthik scope in the final contract language; otherwise call me and we'll hop on a quick 20-min sync.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Exhibit-H_REDLINE_v3.docx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Park <jordan.park@brightpath.ai>, Emily Zhao <emily.z@brightpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Exhibit H redline (internal comments)

Forwarding my edits to the team and BrightPath. I left inline comments in v3 — key legal points below so there's no ambiguity for procurement: 

1) "Adaptive Corridor" vs "Adaptive Cap": I removed the phrase "no reduction below absolute floor" and replaced it with: "Adaptive Corridor shall be calculated using the greater of (a) the prorated SKU baseline for the billing period or (b) the rolling 30-day baseline adjusted by the documented conversion factor." This prevents a perverse outcome where a conversion to a more efficient SKU increases BrightPath's minimum spend exposure.

2) Conversion factors must be operationally defined. I added: "Conversion factors shall be published in a Redwood-maintained SKU mapping table and may be updated quarterly with 30 days' notice; updates shall not apply retroactively." This protects both sides.

3) Invoicing & dispute: I tightened dispute language to "60 days from invoice date" for true-up disputes and added an escalation path that involves ops (Laura) before legal.

Please review my inline comments in the attached doc. If Mina and Jordan are aligned on the monthly finalization cadence, we'll pull this into the order form for signature.

—Karthik
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Zhao <emily.z@brightpath.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@brightpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit H — SKU attribute reconciliation & pro-rata floor/cap mechanics (redlines)

Mina / Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. BrightPath legal ran the draft overnight. We have two small asks before we sign: 

• Can the conversion factor updates be limited to quarterly windows only (i.e., Redwood may publish but changes take effect at quarter boundaries) instead of "30 days' notice"? This helps our billing ops schedule system updates.

• For the invoice line item name, can we call it "SKU migration true-up" exactly (so our ERP maps it automatically) and include invoice meta-key "sku_migration_id"?

If you agree to those two points, BrightPath will sign the order form and we'll push the DocuSign link by EOD today. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emily Zhao
Senior Procurement Ops, BrightPath Analytics
Procurement: procurement@brightpath.ai
